candidates.title: Exact work lost to energy-basis dephasing at fixed post-damping population
candidates.status: review proposal; no new implementation or measurements
candidates.kind: Mathematical lemma plus small code certificate
candidates.priorUnresolvedGap: Existing grid validates ergotropy values but has not packaged an all-parameter monotonicity/loss bound or handled its degenerate differentiability endpoint in a reusable certificate.
candidates.target: For fixed p_star and coherence magnitude c_star allowed by a qubit state, W(d)=epsilon/2*(2*p_star-1+sqrt((1-2*p_star)^2+4*d^2*|c_star|^2)). Prove 0<=W(1)-W(d)<=epsilon*|c_star|*(1-d) for 0<=d<=1, with strict loss iff d<1 and c_star!=0.
assumptions: Fixed positive energy gap and energy-basis dephasing; p_star does not change during this step.
p_star=(1-gamma)*p+gamma*nu and c_star=sqrt(1-gamma)*c may come from the accepted thermal channel.
Ergotropy permits arbitrary cyclic unitary control; no statement about actual control electricity or restricted-device work.
candidates.mathematicalDeliverable: Short algebraic proof, equality/degeneracy cases and a statement of work accessibility versus unchanged mean energy.
candidates.codeTask: A separately scoped certificate and operator-based check of chosen extraction unitaries; no replacement of the accepted calculator.
candidates.measuredExperiment: Protocol only: repeat state tomography and extraction at a fixed calibrated population while varying dephasing; hardware/access, readout calibration and control-energy measurement are prerequisites. No data collection is currently authorized or presumed available.
acceptance: Prove the continuum inequality algebraically, including c_star=0 and p_star=1/2; do not treat a sampled grid as the proof.
An independently selected finite rational/symmetric set agrees with direct Hermitian eigenvalues and unitary energy extraction.
Keep mean energy unchanged while work decreases under stronger dephasing.
wrongControls: Reject W=E for the diagonal passive p_star=1/4 state.
Expose a derivative implementation that divides by the zero Bloch length at p_star=1/2,d=0.
Reject the assertion that damping itself preserves population when nu differs from p.
candidates.feasibility: Closed-form 2x2 algebra; no external proof adoption or new hardware required for lemma/code.
candidates.estimate: About half a focused day for derivation, implementation and independent review; CPU seconds. Hardware protocol only.
candidates.stopRule: Stop after the algebraic proof and a frozen independent check pass; if restricted controls are required, open a separate model rather than silently reusing ergotropy.

candidates.title: Single-temperature full-cycle resource certificate with explicit reset and correlations
candidates.status: review proposal; no new implementation or measurements
candidates.kind: Mathematical cycle bound plus finite-dimensional ledger
candidates.priorUnresolvedGap: The accepted channel measures signed exchange for one use but omits preparation, bath re-preparation, switching, measurement and reset. A reduced battery state also loses joint correlations needed for a reset claim.
candidates.target: For a fixed finite-dimensional Hamiltonian, one full-rank positive-temperature Gibbs reference tau, and an otherwise closed cycle returning all auxiliary states and correlations, certify total work supplied minus work extracted >=0. Restricted one-qubit corollary: W_erg(Phi(rho)) <= F_beta(rho)-F_beta(tau) <= required preparation work, for Gibbs-preserving Phi.
assumptions: 0<nu<1/2 fixes one bath temperature; H=diag(0,epsilon) and beta*epsilon=log((1-nu)/nu).

No second temperature, inverted bath, unreturned phase reference, consumed measurement record or unrecorded controller resource. If present, record its resource change and abstain from the single-bath claim.
Average-work free-energy bounds are necessary bounds, not a claim of exact finite-copy attainability.
Initial implementation uses the existing equal-gap two-qubit exchange dilation with d=1; dephasing/controller environments may be added only when their bookkeeping is explicit.
The joint reset state includes correlations: F(omega_SB)=F(omega_S)+F(omega_B)+k_B*T*I(S:B) for a noninteracting endpoint Hamiltonian.
candidates.mathematicalDeliverable: Telescoping nonequilibrium free-energy inequality, explicit one-qubit corollary, and conditions for resource closure.
candidates.codeTask: Record states and energy/entropy/free-energy changes across preparation, exchange, local extraction and joint reset. Include mutual information and lower bounds on signed reset work; do not assume resetting must always cost positive work or silently set its hardware cost to zero.
candidates.measuredExperiment: A calibrated one-cycle protocol and accounting schema only. Actual control/preparation/refrigeration/switching meters and state reconstructions are needed before any apparatus-efficiency estimate. Missing channels must return incomplete ledger, not a numeric efficiency.
acceptance: Prove the finite-dimensional free-energy identity and its telescoping cycle bound before using a sweep.
For the declared one-qubit channel, verify W_erg <= deltaF_preparation on independently frozen ordinary-bath examples.
For the joint two-qubit model, account for every endpoint and correlation term; show resetting marginals alone is not joint closure.
Allow a signed reset-work bound and explicit heat/entropy exchange; distinguish mathematical lower bounds from measured cost.
A complete ledger can support the bound, while an incomplete ledger returns abstention with missing ports listed.
wrongControls: Omit bath re-preparation and obtain an apparent repeatable gain; ledger must flag a missing operation/resource.
Set nu>1/2 or use two different temperatures but label it a single ordinary bath; reject the premise rather than the physical possibility of driven work.
Replace a correlated joint state by the product of its marginals without recording the lost mutual-information free energy.
Identify a preparation lower bound with measured or necessarily attainable hardware energy.
candidates.feasibility: At most4x4 matrices and established finite-dimensional free-energy identities; useful completion of the existing ledger without attempting channel capacity or new thermodynamics.
candidates.estimate: One to two focused days for a bounded MVP and independent review; no hardware purchase required. Full apparatus measurement depends on external lab access.
candidates.stopRule: Stop with a conditional mathematical certificate and explicit incomplete-hardware status. Do not optimize an efficiency until all physical input/reset channels are measured.

candidates.title: Thermal bosonic beam-splitter bridge and a correlated-input countercontrol
candidates.status: optional review proposal; no new implementation or measurements
candidates.kind: Restricted Gaussian lemma plus covariance validation
candidates.priorUnresolvedGap: Family273 has no current bosonic-mode counterpart in the repository; product-input hypotheses and entropy photon number could otherwise be confused with real generated energy.
candidates.target: For two independent same-frequency thermal bosonic inputs with means N_A,N_B>=0, show a passive beam splitter yields N_C=eta*N_A+(1-eta)*N_B and N_D=(1-eta)*N_A+eta*N_B, preserves total energy, and saturates the thermal EPnI special case. Exhibit a physical correlated input with identical thermal marginals that violates the product-input conclusion when that premise is omitted.
assumptions: One mode per port, same frequency, finite mean number, passive beam splitter and no pump port.
Independent thermal inputs for the equality statement; the correlated countercontrol is deliberately outside that premise.
Quadratures use vacuum covariance I/2; all modeled Gaussian covariances must satisfy the uncertainty relation.
No claim about non-Gaussian inputs, arbitrary multimode EPnI, capacity or a quantum-to-classical sound conversion.
candidates.mathematicalDeliverable: Covariance proof for thermal product inputs and an analytic correlated coherent-mixture countercontrol: a=alpha,b=-alpha with complex Gaussian alpha, balanced sum port vacuum and other port mean2N.
candidates.codeTask: Small4x4 covariance model with symplectic, uncertainty, total-energy and thermal-entropy checks; avoid claiming that a finite Fock cutoff certifies infinite-dimensional entropy.
candidates.measuredExperiment: A thermal-light/beam-splitter protocol could later measure output powers and covariances with independently calibrated ports; correlated RF-noise cancellation is only a classical energy-accounting analogue and must not be reported as a quantum entropy measurement. No apparatus is assumed available.
acceptance: Prove product-thermal equality using g(N)=(N+1)log(N+1)-NlogN and the output thermal marginals.
Check symplectic beam-splitter maps, covariance positivity/uncertainty and total power conservation.
For correlated marginals with N>0 and eta=1/2, demonstrate N_C=0 while the product-input RHS=N; label the failed independence assumption.
Keep frequency conversion/pumped cases outside the passive same-frequency certificate.
wrongControls: Drop cross-covariance and falsely classify the correlated input as a product.
Count destructive interference at one port as missing energy while ignoring the second output.
Use sub-vacuum isotropic covariance as a physical thermal state; uncertainty gate must reject.
candidates.feasibility: Gaussian covariance algebra is closed form; it tests a precise missing premise without depending on the unreviewed full EPnI proof. Lower priority than closing the existing thermal ledger.
candidates.estimate: One focused day for a restricted module/proof and independent review; experimental realization separately gated.
candidates.stopRule: Stop at the thermal Gaussian special case and its countercontrol. Any non-Gaussian/Fock extension requires a new input-energy and truncation-error contract.
